title: Sparkle, Muffin, and the Mayor's Petunias
markdown:
Mist swirled around Oakhaven like a grumpy ghost, hiding sharp edges and softening slate roofs. Watchtowers stood sentinel on the slope. In a study crammed with scrolls that smelled of parchment and dried herbs, Wizard Cassian kept neat habits and robes that hinted he had once meant to be braver. Muffin, his shaggy goat, added her own aroma and was currently redecorating an ancient tapestry with enthusiastic nibbles.

“Oh, Muffin,” Cassian sighed, a whisper of turning pages.

His problem was not the goat, bless her woolly heart. His problem was Sparkle: a stone found on a ridge where stars spilled into a silent lake. It shimmered with a gentle inner light, a contentment that matched Cassian’s quieter hours. He loved Sparkle. He loved Muffin too, even when tapestries became snacks.

“Where has that little flicker gone?” He peered under dusty tomes. Sparkle usually glowed from some shadowed nook. Today, nothing. Then Muffin gave a peculiar contented bleat, followed by a faint fizz from outside. Cassian’s heart sank. Muffin’s favourite hiding spots were always the most inconvenient, and she had a well-known taste for Mayor Grummel’s prize petunias, planted with militant precision before the polished town hall.

He took his best cloak and finest stick. The debate in his head was a tempest in a teacup: companion versus civic order. He could already see the signs. No Unscheduled Nibbling. Petunia Protection Zone. Fines For Unlicensed Leaf-Consumption.

Paths vanished into mist like mischievous sprites. Muffin gave him a grand tour of every damp hollow and interesting moss. “Are you quite certain this is the way?” Cassian asked, injecting encouragement. Muffin wagged. She was enjoying the expedition.

They emerged near the hall. Mayor Grummel, frown etched deep, was lecturing pigeons on proper loafing. His petunias stood in violent pink and indignant purple. Peeking among them, emitting a faint joyful shimmer, was Sparkle. Muffin nudged it closer with a triumphant bleat.

“Aha,” Cassian said, quieter than he meant.

The Mayor’s head snapped. Outrage gathered. “Wizard Cassian! And that!” He pointed not at Cassian but at Muffin. “My prize petunias! Accosted!”

“She seems to have borrowed Sparkle,” Cassian offered, hands raised. “A particularly shiny berry, I imagine. Her eye for shine is exceptional.”

The Mayor’s jowls quivered. “A menace to horticulture! To public order!” Polished boots clicked. “Stricter regulations! No unsupervised animals! And that—” he jabbed at Sparkle, whose shimmer dimmed—“is contraband horticultural decoration!”

Cassian thought fast. Whispers spoke of Ignis, the dragon librarian in the echoing archives above, particular about books, more impressive than frightening.

“Perhaps a visit to the esteemed Ignis is in order. Historical precedents. Rock-related horticultural incidents. Companion management.”

Mayor Grummel, who respected an authority with a title, puffed. “One hour, Wizard. Or you and the beast face the full penalty of No Unscheduled Nibbling. The rock shall be confiscated as evidence.”

The climb to the Great Library was steeper and mistier than hoped. Muffin trotted with unusual solemnity. Ignis was magnificent: obsidian scales, ember eyes, a tome the size of a small wagon balanced on her snout, wings tucked.

“Soot is the bane of my existence,” she rumbled, grinding-stone voice. “A single speck undoes centuries. What do you want, Wizard? And what, pray, is that?” She eyed Muffin. A puff of smoke.

“A predicament. Muffin acquires things. The Mayor is upset about petunias. Specifically about this.” Cassian presented Sparkle.

Ignis blinked. “A stone. Mundane. Potentially messy. This beast has not sullied my manuscripts?”

“Contained,” Cassian said, patting Muffin. “He threatens to ban all animal companions. I cannot imagine life without Muffin. Or Sparkle. They’re my family.”

Ignis snorted. “Family. Often overlooked in the pursuit of pristine parchment. What did the Mayor’s signs say?”

Cassian recounted the alarming pronouncements. A flicker of amusement lived in ancient eyes. “Rigid protocol. I recall a Third Age case: a misplaced griffin feather and an orderly gnome who worshipped aligned garden gnomes.” A dry chuckle ruffled pages. “That Mayor is trying to be subtle. It is not his strongest subject.”

She pointed a claw to a dim section. “He values order and signs. There is a volume: The Principles of Unimpeachable Municipal Management. Emphatic. Diagrams. Very neat.” A weary sigh. “And a small illuminated scroll. Companionable Conduct. Obedience, cleanliness, minimal botanical disruption. Drafted by a dragon librarian of impeccable handwriting.”

They returned armed. Mayor Grummel paced like a thundercloud. “One hour is up!”

“Mayor.” Cassian’s voice held. He lifted Sparkle. “A solution for exacting standards.” He offered the tome. “Excellent methods for keeping everything in its proper place. Even sections on errant flora.”

The Mayor snatched it. His frown deepened over immaculate flowerbed diagrams.

“And this decree, from Ignis herself, on proper conduct for companions. Tidiness. Respect for civic greenery. A deep appreciation for well-preserved literature.”

Ignis had materialized at the entrance, a book-loving mountain. The Mayor’s grumbles thinned.

“A decree. By a dragon. And a book on management. Potential.” He squinted at Muffin, who tried to nudge a polished boot. “Still rather goat-like. Prone to unscheduled nibbling.”

Sparkle pulsed warm. Muffin nudged the stone, then looked at Cassian with earnest goat eyes.

“Muffin is my companion,” Cassian said, clear. “She appreciates nature in her own way. Sparkle is contentment you can hold. Together they bring a kind of balance. A heart, Mayor, is worth keeping organised and well-loved.” He added, practical as a catalogue card, that Sparkle’s light might help the petunias bloom, and that Muffin, under Ignis’s eye, could learn a boundary.

Mayor Grummel gazed at the radiance and the diagrams and, at last, past the flowers. “Very well. Your companions may remain. The decree shall stand. Ignis shall oversee Muffin’s horticultural education. And you, beast,” he told Muffin, who immediately butted his boot, “shall learn the meaning of Petunia Protection Zone.”

Back in the study the tapestry was a little more frayed. Muffin eyed a plump new one with professional interest. Sparkle sat on the sill, evening light in its quiet glow. Cassian stroked the goat, then lifted the stone, familiar warmth in the palm. The mist outside went on being a grumpy ghost. Inside, the family fitted: wizard, goat, stone, and a dragon’s decree that smelled faintly of soot-free ink.
characters: Cassian (wizard of neat habits), Muffin (shaggy goat companion), Ignis (a dragon librarian who dislikes soot on the books)
audience: children aged 9-10, amusing fantasy story for middle-grade readers
author: StoryGen Community
